title: Inspect the Brief's Reusable Structure
scenario: It is 6:50 AM. Every artifact the brief needs now exists. Before assembling, look at the one thing that does NOT change each morning: the brief's structure. Yesterday's brief, the day before's, and today's all share it - that sharing is the lesson.
input:
# Meridian Morning Market Brief - <day>
Status: <approval line>

## Headline
<the hub that moved most, and by how much>

## Hub Summary
<one line per hub: peak, settled, vs forecast>

## Operations
<generation and operational notes>

Same sections, every day. The numbers change; the structure does not. Structure version: 1.0.0, owned by the Desk Manager.
instructions: Read the template and notice what is fixed and what is a placeholder.

questions.prompt: What does this template carry from day to day?

options.text: Structure - the sections every brief must have, in order
The threshold values the desk agreed

questions.explain: Look at what is literal in the input versus what sits in angle brackets: the headings are fixed; every number is a placeholder. The template carries the fixed part.

questions.prompt: The Prior Day Reference also carries something across days. What is the difference?

options.text: There is no difference - they are the same node drawn twice
The reference carries DATA (yesterday's numbers); the template carries STRUCTURE (the sections)
The template carries data; the reference carries structure

questions.explain: Both cross midnight, but they carry different cargo: the baseline feeds Variance Check with numbers; this template feeds the Morning Brief with shape.

questions.prompt: Why does a consistent structure matter beyond looking tidy?

options.text: Readers and downstream automation both know where to look - the Approval line or Headline is always in the same place
It avoids the need for approvals

questions.explain: Consistency is an interface: a manager scans the same spot daily, and anything parsing the brief (like tomorrow's baseline extraction) depends on sections staying put.

questions.prompt: Which workflow step consumes this template?

options.text: Morning Brief - it renders today's values into these sections
Variance Check - it compares against the sections
Approval Decision - it routes based on the headings

questions.explain: Follow the map: the assembly step is where fixed structure meets today's values.

artifactOnPass.distinctFrom: prior-day-reference carries data; this carries structure

copilotPrompt: Profile this output template: what it carries across runs, how it differs from a data baseline, why structural consistency matters, and which step consumes it.
successMessage: Structure verified. The assembly step now has its frame - next you fill it with today's values.

intro.heading: Before you inspect: structure vs data

sections.title: Rendered, not written
sections.body: Nobody authors the brief from scratch at 6:50 AM. The structure already exists; the morning supplies values. Fixed structure plus flowing values is templating - the same pattern behind mail merge, report generators, and every recurring dashboard.

sections.title: Two carriers cross midnight
sections.body: Yesterday hands today two things: numbers (the prior-day baseline, used by Variance Check) and shape (this template, used by assembly). They look like twins on the map; they do different jobs.

sections.title: Structure is an interface
sections.body: Because the Approval line is always at the top, the Desk Manager checks it in one glance - and automation extracting tomorrow's baseline knows where the numbers live. Consistency serves both audiences at once.

sections.title: Structure is governed too
sections.body: The template has a version and an owner, like the Threshold Policy and the Approval Template. Changing the brief's sections is a governance act - readers and parsers both depend on it.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd keep last issue's brief as a starting template so today's edition follows the same headings and order.

tools.powerAutomate: a stored Word/HTML template populated with dynamic content
tools.zapier: a template message step with merge fields for each section
tools.python: a Jinja2 or string template with named sections

takeaway.heading: Structure verified
points: You separated the fixed part of a recurring output (sections) from the flowing part (values).
You can now tell the two midnight-crossing inputs apart: baseline carries data, template carries structure.
You saw structure as an interface serving two audiences: human readers and downstream parsing.
The Morning Brief task renders today's artifacts into exactly these sections.
The workflow can now assemble the daily output against a consistent brief structure.
